public_rationale: Acher's September 30, 2023 report records illegal moves in 72 of 73 games with text-davinci-003 [e1]. His January 22, 2025 report documents repeated illegal moves by DeepSeek-R1, a model from another provider [e2]. These reports establish recurrence across 2023 and 2025, before the June 28, 2025 publication cutoff, and extend the observed problem beyond ChatGPT [e1, e2]. They support the claim about unreliable chess behavior, without establishing that absent internal world models caused it [e1, e2].
limitations: Both reports come from the same investigator [e1, e2].
The game records establish recurrence, not prevalence across all LLMs or a shared internal cause [e1, e2].

statement.excerpt: This is not just a problem with ChatGPT, by the way. The problem has been around for years.

our_interpretation: In context, the observable problem is unreliable chess play, including illegal moves and board-tracking failures.
Persistence means documented recurrence across years, not failure by every model in every game.
Beyond ChatGPT requires another identifiable model or system. Evidence from a different provider is especially clear.
The context explicitly anchors the historical comparison in 2023; use January 1, 2023 through June 28, 2025.
This assessment does not treat persistent illegal moves as proof that internal world models are absent.
criteria.support_condition: Dated primary tests document chess-rule or board-tracking failures in 2023 and again before publication in 2025, including a system beyond ChatGPT.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Comparable historical records establish that the alleged failures did not recur across those years or were confined to ChatGPT.
